key_insight: CalTennis introduces a very large, real-world tennis video benchmark for testing monocular-to-3D pose estimation under challenging in-the-wild conditions. Its synchronized multi-camera setup and scale make it a stronger evaluation resource than prior datasets.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of large, realistic, multi-view datasets with reliable ground truth for evaluating how well monocular-to-3D pose methods perform outside controlled lab settings.
method: Collected over 11 million frames (51 hours) of tennis practice and match play from 40 players.
Captured each session with 2-6 synchronized cameras at 60 Hz to enable multi-view analysis and stronger 3D pose supervision/evaluation.
Built a benchmark focused on monocular-to-3D pose estimation in real-world sports motion, with dataset scale exceeding prior in-the-wild and MOCAP-ground-truthed datasets.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CalTennis provides a more realistic and scalable benchmark for measuring generalization, robustness, and failure modes of 3D pose estimation systems. It can help drive better models for sports analytics, human motion understanding, and real-world deployment.
